our_title: Dead common_error.c compiled into the CMake libScotch, exporting un-prefixed errorPrint/errorPrintW/errorProg
ran: nm -D cm/base32/lib/libscotch.so | grep -E ' [TU] (errorPrint|errorPrintW|errorProg|SCOTCH_errorPrint)$' -> 'U SCOTCH_errorPrint', 'T errorPrint', 'T errorPrintW', 'T errorProg'; Makefile build (INFRA/asan/lib/libscotch.so): only the U lines. grep -n common_error src/libscotch/Makefile -> nothing; git log -S common_error -- src/libscotch/Makefile -> nothing (added to CMake only, e79c930). Patched: no T errorP* in libscotch.so.
evidence: src/libscotch/CMakeLists.txt:211 '  common_error.c'; common_error.c:89 'errorPrint (' defining a global, un-renamed routine never called by the library (module.h renames only SCOTCH_errorPrint).

fix_options.label: a: remove the file and its entry
fix_options.summary: git rm src/libscotch/common_error.c; drop it from SCOTCH_C_SOURCES.
fix_options.tested: patched builds, nm, ctest 181/181, ci/check_sources.sh rc=0.
fix_options.tradeoffs: None: the file is referenced nowhere else.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: He deletes what is unused ('Remove useless structure definition' in the 7.0.17 range).

fix_options.label: b: keep the file, drop the CMake entry
fix_options.tested: untested as a tree (subset of a).
fix_options.tradeoffs: Leaves a dead file that the checker script would not flag but IDEs and sonar would.

our_title: symbol_fax.c compiled standalone by the CMake build of libEsMUMPS, exporting an un-prefixed symbolFax
ran: nm -D cm/base32/lib/libesmumps.so | grep -i symbolfax -> 'T _ESMUMPSsymbolFaxGraph' and 'T symbolFax'; Makefile build (make esmumps in the ASan tree, build/lib/libesmumps.so): only _ESMUMPSsymbolFaxGraph. Patched CMake build: only _ESMUMPSsymbolFaxGraph.
evidence: src/esmumps/CMakeLists.txt:76-77 '  symbol_fax_graph.c\n  symbol_fax.c)'; symbol_fax_graph.c:131 '#include "symbol_fax.c"'; esmumps/Makefile LIBESMUMPSDEPS ends with 'symbol_fax_graph$(OBJ)' and :196 lists symbol_fax.c as a dependency only.

fix_options.label: a: remove it from esmumps_src
fix_options.summary: The compiler's dependency scanning tracks the include.
fix_options.tested: patched builds; nm; libesmumps consumer link via SCOTCH::esmumps not tested separately (esmumps has no src/check test).

fix_options.label: b: mark it HEADER_FILE_ONLY
fix_options.summary: set_source_files_properties(symbol_fax.c PROPERTIES HEADER_FILE_ONLY ON) and keep it listed.
fix_options.tradeoffs: Keeps the file visible in IDEs at the cost of a property nobody else in the tree uses.

our_title: Misspelt dependency rules in src/libscotch/Makefile (arch_vcpmlt, library_arch_dom -> library_arch.c)
ran: awk scan of 'x$(OBJ) : y.c' rules with x != y -> :800 arch_vcpmlt builds arch_vcmplt.c; :2171 library_arch_dom builds library_arch.c (library_error_pt/_exit_pt are intentional). Pristine tree: touch arch_vcmplt.h; make -n arch_vcmplt.o -> nothing (object not rebuilt). Patched Makefile tree: recompiles arch_vcmplt.c; make -j4 scotch ptscotch esmumps: rc 0, 0 warnings in the 32-bit ASan tree and the INTSIZE64 tree; make check (sequential suite, 50 check_* rules): no error.
evidence: src/libscotch/Makefile:800 'arch_vcpmlt$(OBJ)\t\t:\tarch_vcmplt.c' (phantom target; arch_vcmplt.o only gets the %$(OBJ): %.c pattern rule, :85, so header edits do not rebuild it); :2171 'library_arch_dom$(OBJ)\t\t:\tlibrary_arch.c' (spurious prerequisite; the object is still compiled from library_arch_dom.c because $< of a pattern rule is the pattern's own prerequisite).

fix_options.label: a: fix the two names
fix_options.maintainer_fit: A typo fix; the Makefile dependency rules are hand-maintained (5efb923 adds one by hand).

fix_options.label: b: compiler-generated dependencies
fix_options.summary: Add -MMD -MP to the pattern rule and -include *.d, making the hand-written rules redundant (and fix the typos meanwhile).
fix_options.tested: untested: structural; requires a compiler supporting -MMD (not NMake/pgcc guaranteed).
fix_options.tradeoffs: Would remove 2000 lines of hand-written rules eventually, but is a design decision and portability question for the maintainer.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Out of scope for a typo; the maintainer keeps explicit rules for portability.

our_title: CMake build with SCOTCH_NAME_SUFFIX and ENABLE_TESTS=ON fails to link test_scotch_mesh_build_f (calls not suffixed)
ran: cmake -S src-base -B cm/suffix32 -DSCOTCH_NAME_SUFFIX=_pys -DBUILD_SHARED_LIBS=ON ... && make -j4 -> 'Linking Fortran executable ../../bin/test_scotch_mesh_build_f ... undefined reference to scotchfmeshinit_' and 'scotchfmeshbuild_', build rc=2 (default ENABLE_TESTS=ON). Same template in 7.0.17 (src/check/test_scotch_mesh_build_f.f90.in exists there). With -DENABLE_TESTS=OFF the suffixed build succeeds. Not patched here: src/check templates belong to G30 (BLD-09/BLD-10).
evidence: test_scotch_mesh_build_f.f90.in:71 '  call scotchfmeshinit(meshdat, ierr)' written literally, whereas test_libmetis_dual_f.f90.in:98 writes '  call SCOTCHMETISNAMEFU (METIS_MeshToDual) (...)' which dummysizes -s rewrites; the generated cm/suffix32/src/check/test_scotch_mesh_build_f.f90:71 still reads 'call scotchfmeshinit(meshdat, ierr)' while the library exports scotchfmeshinit_pys_.

fix_options.label: a: write the calls through the name macro
fix_options.summary: Use the dummysizes name-substitution form (as test_libmetis_dual_f.f90.in does) for scotchfmeshinit/scotchfmeshbuild/... in test_scotch_mesh_build_f.f90.in.
fix_options.tested: untested: not written (G30's file); the metis template proves the mechanism links under a suffix (test_libmetis_dual_f built in the same run).
fix_options.tradeoffs: None once the macro form is used; the Makefile check (src/check/Makefile:578-582) compiles the same template so it must keep working there.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Consistent with the other Fortran template.

fix_options.label: b: skip Fortran tests when a suffix is set
fix_options.summary: if(USE_SUFFIX) do not add the Fortran tests.
fix_options.tradeoffs: Hides the gap; suffixed Fortran API stays untested.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: He would rather fix the test.
